messages:
lee_support: FYI — ACME reported a sudden p99 jump (~4x) on /v1/generate starting ~08:10 UTC, customer sees timeouts. Ticket INC-4532. Root traces show a pileup at ingress/admits. Attaching repro

megan_sre: Thanks Lee. Are they on Hosted or Dedicated? Any tenant id or sample trace/span id?

lee_support: Hosted (prod). Tenant: acme-corp. Sample trace id: 9f7a2c1b. Quick repro curl I used:```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"summarize: long doc...","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```customer says p95 also degraded but p99 is worst.

tim_runtime: I'm seeing a spike in ingress.pending_requests and admit_queue_length for the acme tenant starting 08:09. Worker pool for region-us-east-1 hit max_inflight and CPU for model-gpt-large is at 92%. Logs show repeated `admit: reject=concurrency_limit` entries.

anika_prod: Can we confirm whether prefix/KV cache hit rates changed? Also any recent routing rules that could have funneled more traffic to a single shard?

tim_runtime: Cache hit rate steady. Routing change rolled out yesterday but it was for a different model family. This looks like a sudden burst from a small number of heavy requests — probably long-context jobs.

lee_support: Customer provided a sample payload with 12k tokens. They said they hit this after a batch job started.

megan_sre: Short-term mitigation options: (1) enable tenant-level fallback to smaller model, (2) temporarily raise concurrency cap for acme if capacity exists, (3) enable burstpool warmup or route to other region. Which is safest now?

tim_runtime: We have capacity in us-west-2. Easiest quick action: update admit policy to allow burst routing to us-west-2 and/or set fallback model to gpt-medium-quant at tenant level. I can patch admit policy — will need a quick canary.

anika_prod: If we bump concurrency, we risk starving other tenants on the same shard unless we isolate. Prefer routing to other region + fallback model. Also suggest reducing `max_tokens` for long-context requests temporarily via a soft quota and ask customer to retry with truncated context.

lee_support: Passing recommendations to customer now (fallback model + temporary truncation). They asked if we can do anything server-side right away.

tim_runtime: I'll create a short-lived routing override for acme: `redwood route override --tenant acme-corp --to-region us-west-2 --max-duration 30m` and set fallback: `redwood tenant update acme-corp --fallback-model gpt-medium-quant`

deploy-bot: admit-policy-canary v1.2.3 deployed to 2 nodes in us-east-1 — health checks green :white_check_mark:

megan_sre: Tim, before you push the override, can you also reduce the tenant's max_inflight from 200 -> 150 to avoid sudden increase in queueing after routing? We want to keep p95 reasonable while routing warms up.

tim_runtime: Doing both now. Pushing override + fallback + lowering max_inflight. Commands ran and returned OK. Monitoring ingress.pending_requests and per-tenant latency.

(1m later)

tim_runtime: Update: pending_requests for acme down ~60%, p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s on canary traffic. No regressions in other tenants observed so far.

megan_sre: Nice. Can we add a temporary alert: if acme p99 > 1.5s again fire a paging alert to oncall?

lee_support: Customer confirms latency improved on their end after we applied fallback and asked them to truncate heavy jobs. They're going to stagger the batch.

anika_prod: Longer-term action items: (a) add warmup/elastic burstpool for heavy-token jobs, (b) tenant QoS doc update (guidance for long-context batch jobs), (c) consider tenant-isolated pools for high-SLA customers. I'll add to backlog and tag runtime/ops.

megan_sre: Filing postmortem-lite and linking INC-4532. Will include timelines, mitigations, and config changes.

lee_support: Closing loop with customer and noting actions in ticket. Monitoring window 2h. Thanks team :pray:

megan_sre: Good job everyone. If p99 creeps back up, we'll reopen and escalate to infra.
